title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-wa51: Rust edhoc TH_4 uses CIPHERTEXT_3 instead of PLAINTEXT_3+CRED_I — cross-implementation interop break
description:
## Summary

The commit changes EDHOC TH_4 computation asymmetrically between Python and Rust, creating a hard interop break.

### What Python does (correct per RFC 9528 section 3.4)

- Init TH_4: `H(TH_3, PLAINTEXT_3, CRED_I)` — uses plaintext + credential
- Resp TH_4: `H(TH_3, PLAINTEXT_3, CRED_I)` — same

### What Rust does (wrong)

- Init TH_4 (line 1224): `transcript_4(&th_3, &ciphertext_3.0)` — uses ciphertext only, no credential
- Resp TH_4 (line 1667): `transcript_4(&th_3, &pending.ciphertext_3)` — same
- `transcript_4` function at line 477 only accepts 2 params: `(th_3, ciphertext_3)`

### Impact

Python and Rust implementations will derive different TH_4 values, leading to different OSCORE master secrets, sender/recipient keys. Compromises all interop.

### Root cause

The `transcript_4` function was never updated to RFC 9528's 3-input definition H(TH_3, PLAINTEXT_3, CRED_I). This diff made a bad situation worse: the responder path changed from `plaintext` (closer to correct) to `ciphertext_3` (further from correct).

### Fix needed

1. Update `transcript_4` to accept `(th_3, plaintext_3, credential)` — 3 params
2. Update both call sites (init line 1224, resp line 1667) to pass plaintext + credential
3. Remove the `ciphertext_3` field from `PendingMessage3` — it's not needed for correct TH_4

### Verification

The test at line 1957 already calls `transcript_4(&th_3, &plaintext_3, &credential_i)` with the correct 3-arg signature — proving the function needs 3 params. Build currently fails with `--features edhoc` due to signature mismatch.
